papers.title: Spatiotemporal Multi-Omics Reveals Primate-Specific Mechanisms of Liver Regeneration Following Partial Hepatectomy.
papers.abstract: The liver is a vital metabolic organ with an extraordinary capacity for regeneration, making it a key focus for understanding tissue repair and developing therapeutic strategies for liver diseases. However, ethical limitations restrict liver regeneration research largely to rodents, leaving critical gaps in our understanding of primate-specific mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study uses spatiotemporal multi-omics to profile liver regeneration after partial hepatectomy in a primate model, addressing the gap left by rodent-only research due to ethical constraints. It identifies primate-specific molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying liver regeneration, providing a resource for translational liver biology.

papers.title: A droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing method for the high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within individual cells.
papers.abstract: Recently, long-read sequencing methods have revolutionized genomic research by allowing the resolution of previously inaccessible regions across the genome. However, the throughput and scalability of these methods have hindered their general application in the field. To address this limitation, we developed droplet-based methods for the single-cell profiling of chromatin accessibility (droplet-based single-cell Nanopore ATAC-seq, dscNanoATAC) and histone modifications (droplet-based single-cell NanoCUT&Tag, dscNanoCUT) by combining a commercial microfluidic device and long-read sequencing plat
papers.summary: The authors developed droplet-based long-read single-cell methods, dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT, that combine a commercial microfluidic device with nanopore sequencing to profile chromatin accessibility and histone modifications in individual cells at high throughput. This addresses the scalability bottleneck of prior long-read single-cell epigenomic approaches, enabling multidimensional regulatory element profiling per cell.

papers.title: Stromal CCL2/CXCL10/SPARC axes drive pro-tumor CHI3L1 expression for microenvironmental modulation in pancreatic cancer progression and therapeutic innovation.
papers.abstract: Chitinase-3-like-protein 1 (CHI3L1), a low-abundance protein in normal tissues, is markedly upregulated in the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), where it promotes fibrosis and immune evasion. Spatial transcriptomics revealed enrichment of CHI3L1 at tumor-stroma interfaces, suggesting that cell-cell interactions regulate CHI3L1 expression.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to show that CHI3L1, a pro-fibrotic and immunosuppressive protein, is enriched at tumor-stroma interfaces in pancreatic cancer. The authors identify stromal CCL2, CXCL10, and SPARC as signals that drive CHI3L1 expression, highlighting these axes as potential therapeutic targets for modulating the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies SLCO1B3 as a prognostic marker and functional oncogenic driver in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a leading cause of cancer mortality with limited prognostic biomarkers. Given the role of metabolic reprogramming in tumor progression, this study investigated the clinical relevance and biological function of the lipid metabolism-associated transporter SLCO1B3 in HNSCC.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to show that the lipid metabolism transporter SLCO1B3 is a prognostic marker in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Functional experiments further indicate SLCO1B3 acts as an oncogenic driver, linking metabolic reprogramming to tumor progression.

papers.title: Mid-zone hepatocytes trade proliferation for survival via Atf4-Chop axis in early acute liver injury.
papers.abstract: Hepatocytes undergo extensive proliferation to facilitate liver repair after injury, yet early adaptive changes prior to proliferation remain unclear. Using a mouse model of acetaminophen (APAP)-induced liver injury, we show that hepatocytes undergo transient proliferation suppression that is most pronounced in mid-zone hepatocytes, consistent with zonal APAP metabolism. Although spatial transcriptomics (ST) alone could not independently confirm zonal proliferative restraint, ST analysis identified a unique mid-zone stress-response program centered on the Atf4-Chop axis. By integrating Cut&Run
papers.summary: Using a mouse model of acetaminophen-induced liver injury, this study shows that hepatocytes in the mid-zone of the liver lobule transiently suppress proliferation early after injury, matching the zonal pattern of APAP metabolism. Spatial transcriptomics revealed a mid-zone stress-response program centered on the Atf4-Chop axis, suggesting these cells prioritize survival over proliferation during the early adaptive phase.

papers.title: CCCView: A Knowledge Platform for Integrated Analysis of Spatial Transcriptomic Cell-Cell Communication.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables investigation of cell-cell communication (CCC) while preserving spatial context, yet large-scale resources that organize spatial CCC results across studies and make them readily searchable, visualizable, and comparable remain limited. Here, we present CCCView, a knowledge platform integrating 699 spatial transcriptomics samples and 7,473,444 inferred CCC interactions across 24 tissues, 182 annotated cell types, and 27 biological conditions in human and mouse. CCCView uses a unified cell-type annotation workflow and organizes results from three complementary CCC-
papers.summary: CCCView is a new knowledge platform that aggregates cell-cell communication (CCC) results inferred from 699 spatial transcriptomics samples, covering 7.47 million interactions across 24 tissues, 182 cell types, and 27 biological conditions in human and mouse. It applies a unified cell-type annotation workflow and organizes results from three complementary CCC inference methods, making spatial CCC data searchable, visualizable, and comparable across studies. This addresses the current lack of large-scale, integrated resources for spatial CCC analysis.

papers.title: Serial Cryosectioning for the Spatial Transcriptomics of Plant Tissues.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while preserving tissue architecture, making it a powerful approach for studying plant developmental transitions. However, preparing small and structurally complex plant tissues for spatial transcriptomics remains technically challenging because samples must be rapidly preserved, precisely oriented, serially sectioned, and accurately positioned within the limited capture area of the Visium slides. Here, we describe an optimized workflow for cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement, and data analysis of small
papers.summary: This protocol describes an optimized workflow for preparing small, structurally complex plant tissues for 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics, covering cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement on capture slides, and downstream data analysis. It addresses the practical challenges of rapid preservation, precise orientation, and accurate positioning within the limited capture area, making spatial transcriptomics more accessible for plant developmental studies.

papers.title: A Cross-Condition Single-Cell Atlas Defines Skeletal Muscle Adaptation and Its Predictive Limits.
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle adapts to diverse stresses through coordinated changes across myofibres and cellular niches, yet these responses are usually studied separately. We assembled a cross-species discovery atlas of 501,940 cells and nuclei from six public resources, comprising 2863 condition-time-state combinations defined at the declared analysis unit level, and evaluated it with two independent validation datasets. Injury produced the largest observed compositional displacement, followed by mechanical overload, whereas acute human endurance exercise and denervation showed smaller occupancy shifts
papers.summary: This study assembled a large cross-species single-cell atlas of skeletal muscle (501,940 cells/nuclei from six public resources, covering 2,863 condition-time-state combinations) to compare how muscle adapts to different stresses. Injury caused the largest compositional shifts, followed by mechanical overload, while acute endurance exercise and denervation produced smaller changes. The atlas also probes the predictive limits of using such data to infer adaptation.

papers.title: Meta-Analysis of ALS Post-Mortem Cerebral Cortex Transcriptome Studies Identifies Robust Shifts in Gene Expression Despite Significant Between-Study Heterogeneity.
papers.abstract: Background: ALS is characterized by motor neuron failure with potential neurocognitive comorbidity. Cortical neurons, and their support cells, exhibit pathologic features, some of which have been identified in post-mortem transcriptome studies of the cortex from ALS patients and control subjects. These studies, however, have utilized varying technologies with few attempts to reconcile findings. Methods: This study used meta-analysis to evaluate differential gene expression (ALS vs. control) from 16 prior transcriptome studies utilizing multiple technologies (microarray, bulk RNA-seq or snRNA-s
papers.summary: This meta-analysis integrated 16 post-mortem cerebral cortex transcriptome studies of ALS patients versus controls, spanning microarray, bulk RNA-seq, and snRNA-seq technologies. Despite substantial between-study heterogeneity, the authors identified robust and reproducible shifts in gene expression, supporting a consensus cortical transcriptomic signature in ALS.

papers.title: CDState Resolves Malignant Cell Heterogeneity from Bulk Tumor RNA Sequencing Data.
papers.abstract: Intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity (ITTH), defined as the coexistence of diverse cell states within a single tumor, complicates cancer treatment and contributes to variable therapeutic responses. Although single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can resolve this complexity, its cost and technical demands limit large-scale use. Bulk RNA-seq provides a scalable alternative but requires computational methods to deconvolve bulk transcriptomes into distinct cell states. Existing supervised approaches rely on accurate reference data, which are lacking for many cancer types, whereas unsupervised
papers.summary: CDState is a computational method that deconvolves bulk tumor RNA sequencing data to resolve intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity into distinct malignant cell states without requiring supervised reference data. This enables scalable characterization of cell-state diversity across many cancer types where single-cell data are unavailable or impractical.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omic Analysis of Paired Primary and Peritoneal Metastatic Tumors Reveals GPAA1 as a Therapeutic Target in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Peritoneal metastasis confers a dismal prognosis in colorectal cancer (CRC-PM), with median survival rarely exceeding 20 months. Here we employed multi-omic profiling to identify actionable drivers of CRC-PM. We performed whole-exome sequencing (WES) and label-free quantitative proteomics on 13 and 7 matched primary-peritoneal metastasis pairs, respectively. Public single-cell (GSE183916 and GSE132465) and spatial transcriptomic datasets (GSE225857) were integrated to dissect cellular heterogeneity. TCGA cohorts were used for survival analysis, and functional validation was performed in DLD1 c
papers.summary: This study combined whole-exome sequencing and proteomics on matched primary and peritoneal metastatic colorectal cancer samples, then integrated public single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data to identify drivers of metastasis. The authors pinpoint GPAA1 as a potential therapeutic target for peritoneal metastasis, supported by survival analyses in TCGA and functional validation in cell lines. The work provides a multi-omic resource and candidate target for a poorly prognosed CRC subtype.

papers.title: CQRM: A Composite Quantile Regression Model for Differential Expression Analysis of Non-Coding RNA Count Data.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) play important roles in various biological processes, primarily via regulating gene expression at multiple levels. Nevertheless, compared to protein-coding genes, ncRNAs are relatively understudied. They are characterized by low expression, large variation, and more dynamic expression across different tissues and cell types, which creates unique challenges in differential expression (DE) analysis. Methods: We propose the CQRM, an adaptive multi-quantile testing framework for ncRNA count data that incorporates jittering to accommodate discrete cou
papers.summary: The authors propose CQRM, a composite quantile regression framework for differential expression analysis of non-coding RNA count data. It uses adaptive multi-quantile testing with jittering to handle the discrete, low-expression, and highly variable nature of ncRNA counts, addressing limitations of standard DE methods for this data type.

papers.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
papers.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from c
papers.summary: This review synthesizes knowledge about the tenocyte (the tendon-building cell) and its collagen matrix as a single integrated system spanning eight orders of magnitude in scale. It organizes the field around five causal transitions, from collagen chemistry through molecular mechanics, fibril and fascicle assembly, tissue loading, cellular mechanotransduction, and transcriptional response. The authors argue that chemical, physical, biological, and mathematical descriptions of tendon have developed in separate literatures and need to be unified.

papers.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
papers.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic
papers.summary: The authors developed a method to isolate intact multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) from the spleens of mice chronically infected with Leishmania donovani, overcoming the difficulty of recovering these cells from tissue. They then profiled the transcriptome of these MGCs, providing the first gene expression signature for this cell type in the context of visceral leishmaniasis. This work offers a resource for understanding how MGCs may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated risk program for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary metastasis/relapse (PM/R) is a major cause of osteosarcoma treatment failure. We aimed to develop a compact transcriptomic PM/R risk score and characterize associated immune and single-cell programs.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to build a compact risk score predicting pulmonary metastasis or relapse in osteosarcoma, identifying a HERC5-linked program associated with immune attenuation. The work links this risk signature to specific immune and single-cell transcriptional programs, offering a potential prognostic tool and biological rationale for immune involvement in osteosarcoma progression.

papers.title: Beyond Histocompatibility: Donor Tissue Immune States and Their Role in Heart Transplantation.
papers.abstract: Heart transplantation transfers not only donor alloantigens and functional myocardium but also a pre-existing tissue environment shaped by resident immune, vascular, stromal, and parenchymal populations. This review examines the hypothesis that the biological state of donor tissue influences subsequent recipient immunity and contributes to heterogeneity in allograft outcomes. Donor-resident macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, and tissue-resident lymphocytes constitute an immunologically active myocardial niche that encounters ischemia-reperfusion injury and recip
papers.summary: This review proposes that donor heart tissue carries an active immune environment—including resident macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and tissue-resident lymphocytes—that shapes how the recipient's immune system responds after transplantation. It argues that this pre-existing donor tissue state, beyond just alloantigen matching, contributes to variability in transplant outcomes and should be considered in donor assessment and post-transplant management.

papers.title: Pan-Cancer Analysis Identifies LUC7L2 as a Prognostic Biomarker and Potential Functional Regulator of Prostate Cancer Progression.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cancer imposes a substantial global public health burden, and its initiation and progression involve complex dysregulation of gene expression regulatory networks. Methods: This study systematically evaluated the expression characteristics and prognostic value of LUC7L2 across pan-cancer types, with a particular focus on functional validation in prostate cancer. Using transcriptomic and proteomic data from multiple databases, immunohistochemical staining from the Human Protein Atlas, and single-cell transcriptomic datasets GSE137829 and GSE176031, we analyzed the expressi
papers.summary: This pan-cancer study shows that LUC7L2 expression is dysregulated across multiple cancer types and is associated with patient prognosis, with particular relevance in prostate cancer. Functional and single-cell analyses suggest LUC7L2 may actively regulate prostate cancer progression rather than merely serving as a passive marker. The work nominates LUC7L2 as a candidate prognostic biomarker and possible therapeutic target.

papers.title: Scalable localization of clustering instability for spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Standard spatial transcriptomics workflows rely on clustering methods to define regions of interest for down-stream analyses, such as differential expression and pathway enrichment. Although researchers are presented with a single partition, most clustering methods are stochastic, meaning their output depends on random algorithmic choices, typically controlled by a seed; thus, repeating the analysis changing only the seed can yield a different result. Spatial transcriptomics data may be especially sensitive to algorithmic perturbations due to high dimensionality, sparsity, and mixed expression
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces a method to identify where clustering results in spatial transcriptomics are unstable across different random seeds, rather than relying on a single partition. Because spatial transcriptomics data are high-dimensional, sparse, and mixed, clustering can vary substantially with algorithmic randomness, and this tool localizes the unstable regions so researchers can assess reliability. The approach is designed to scale to large spatial datasets.

papers.title: Spathology: The Birth of Spatial Pathology as a Discipline.
papers.abstract: Pathology has always been a spatial science: for more than 150 years, diagnosis has rested on reading the architecture of cells and tissues. Three technological streams are now converging on this founding principle. Spatially resolved omics can measure thousands of transcripts and over a hundred proteins in intact, formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue; multiplexed imaging quantifies tissue microenvironments cell by cell; and computational pathology has progressed from slide digitization to foundation models that can predict molecular features from morphology. The clinical evidence fo
papers.summary: This perspective argues that spatial pathology is emerging as a distinct discipline from the convergence of three technologies: spatially resolved omics (measuring thousands of transcripts and hundreds of proteins in intact FFPE tissue), multiplexed imaging (quantifying tissue microenvironments cell by cell), and computational pathology (foundation models predicting molecular features from morphology). The authors frame pathology's 150-year history of reading tissue architecture as the foundation for this new field.

papers.title: SPP1⁺ macrophage-derived WNT5A contributes to MMP11⁺ myCAF-mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the leading subtype of non-small cell lung cancer. However, the stromal-immune circuits that coordinate matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the stromal-immune interactions associated with LUAD progression and poor response to PD-1 blockade.
papers.summary: This study identifies a stromal-immune circuit in lung adenocarcinoma in which SPP1⁺ macrophages secrete WNT5A to drive MMP11⁺ myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblasts (myCAFs) and matrix remodeling, which in turn promotes resistance to PD-1 blockade. The work links specific macrophage and fibroblast subpopulations to immunotherapy failure, suggesting these cell states and their signaling axes as potential therapeutic targets or biomarkers.

papers.title: Cell-Cell Communication Patterns in Alzheimer's Disease Differ by Cortical Layer.
papers.abstract: Existing cell-cell communication (CCC) studies of Alzheimer's disease dementia (ADD) using cortical snRNAseq data do not account for the distinct cell-type and gene-expression profiles within cortical layers. Cortical-layer-aware CCC analysis may clarify biological mechanisms associated with ADD and mild cognitive impairment (MCI).
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint argues that existing cell-cell communication analyses of Alzheimer's disease using cortical snRNA-seq data ignore the distinct cellular composition and gene expression profiles of individual cortical layers. The authors propose a layer-aware CCC analysis to better resolve biological mechanisms underlying Alzheimer's disease dementia and mild cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Native, Memory-Bounded Conversion of Mass Spectrometry Imaging Data into the SpatialData Ecosystem.
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) is now a routine modality for spatial molecular profiling and is increasingly combined with histology, multiplexed imaging, and spatial transcriptomics to build richer descriptions of tissue than any single technique can provide. The conceptual case for this multimodal paradigm was settled a decade ago, but the data infrastructure needed to operationalize it at scale has not kept up. Vendor binaries and the imzML exchange format keep MSI outside the OME-NGFF, Zarr, and SpatialData stacks on which the rest of spatial omics has converged, leaving each new experime
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry
papers.summary: This paper presents a tool for converting mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data into the SpatialData ecosystem, which is the standard data infrastructure used by other spatial omics modalities. The conversion is native and memory-bounded, meaning it can handle large datasets without excessive memory use. This helps integrate MSI with histology, multiplexed imaging, and spatial transcriptomics for multimodal tissue analysis.

papers.title: NoiBic: a noise-tolerant biclustering algorithm for high-throughput gene expression data analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput transcriptomic technologies generate large-scale gene expression datasets for functional module discovery. However, technical and biological noise can obscure coherent expression patterns and compromise module detection. Noise-tolerant methods are therefore needed to recover meaningful biclusters.
papers.summary: NoiBic is a new biclustering algorithm designed to tolerate noise when identifying coherent gene-expression modules in large transcriptomic datasets. It aims to recover meaningful gene-sample biclusters that would otherwise be obscured by technical and biological noise, improving functional module discovery from high-throughput expression data.

papers.title: PRISM-GEP: Viewing single-cell expression through the lens of topic modeling.
papers.abstract: Gene-expression programs (GEPs) are the co-regulated gene modules whose coordinated activity encodes biological processes. Recovering them from single-cell RNA-seq is hard because regulation is many-to-many. A cell can run several programs at once, and a gene can take part in several. Methods that resolve programs along a trajectory break this structure by assigning each gene to a single program.
papers.summary: PRISM-GEP applies topic modeling to single-cell RNA-seq data to recover gene-expression programs (co-regulated gene modules) without forcing each gene into a single program, preserving the many-to-many structure of gene regulation. This addresses a key limitation of trajectory-based methods that assign genes to one program at a time.

papers.title: Dermatopathology 2030: Navigating the Digital, Computational and Molecular Convergence for Precision Diagnostics-Originated from a Round Table Discussion at A 66, Basel.
papers.abstract: Background: Traditional dermatopathology relies on analog, qualitative pattern recognition, which encounters critical limitations when facing diagnostic "gray zones" and ambiguous tumor proliferations. Objectives: This paper synthesizes a comprehensive framework integrating Whole Slide Imaging (WSI), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and multi-omics to evaluate how this structural convergence redesigns diagnostic risk and safety ecosystems toward 2030. Methods: We analyze the conceptual shift from individual microscope-based observation to multiple data integration. We integrate recent algorithmic
papers.summary: This perspective piece synthesizes a roundtable discussion on how dermatopathology is converging with whole slide imaging, artificial intelligence, and multi-omics to move beyond analog pattern recognition toward integrated precision diagnostics. The authors argue that combining digital slides, algorithms, and molecular data can resolve diagnostic gray zones and ambiguous tumor proliferations, and they outline a framework for redesigning diagnostic risk and safety ecosystems by 2030.

papers.title: Cell-Cell Communication in Embryonic Kidney Development: Insights from Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Embryonic kidney morphogenesis depends on the coordinated communication among ureteric epithelium, nephron progenitors, stroma, endothelium and differentiating nephrons. Classical studies established central roles for glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF) signaling through the RET proto-oncogene receptor tyrosine kinase (RET), WNT-family signaling, fibroblast growth factor (FGF), bone morphogenetic protein (BMP), Notch, Hedgehog, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) pathways, but pathway-centered models do not fully explain why simila
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how single-cell and spatial transcriptomics have refined our understanding of intercellular signaling during embryonic kidney development, moving beyond classical pathway-centered models (GDNF/RET, WNT, FGF, BMP, Notch, Hedgehog, VEGF, PDGF) toward a cell-type-resolved view of communication among ureteric epithelium, nephron progenitors, stroma, endothelium, and differentiating nephrons. It highlights how these technologies reveal the spatial and temporal coordination of signaling that classical approaches could not fully explain.

papers.title: Pan-Cancer Metabolic Landscapes: A Multiomics View.
papers.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming fuels cancer progression, but whether common metabolic patterns exist across diverse malignancies remains incompletely understood. To address this, we integrated large-scale proteomic, transcriptomic [The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)], and spatial transcriptomic (Spatial Meta-Transcriptome Database) data sets comprising 3226 samples across 24 human cancer types. Utilizing a highly controlled, predominantly patient-matched design to minimize background noise, we characterized the pan-cancer metabolic landscape via reaction-level functional task scoring, pathway enrichment,
papers.summary: This study integrated proteomic, transcriptomic (TCGA), and spatial transcriptomic data from 3,226 samples across 24 cancer types to map metabolic reprogramming at a pan-cancer level. Using reaction-level functional task scoring and pathway enrichment, the authors characterized common and cancer-type-specific metabolic patterns. The work provides a multiomics resource for understanding shared metabolic vulnerabilities across malignancies.

papers.title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
papers.abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug se
papers.summary: The authors present CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that first deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and cell-type-specific expression, then uses this to infer drug sensitivity from bulk transcriptomes. This enables drug response prediction that accounts for cellular heterogeneity rather than treating bulk samples as homogeneous.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of CARGs is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat, and CARG activi
papers.summary: This study combined single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from public repositories to characterize the expression of cell adhesion-related genes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors identify gene signatures associated with adhesion pathways that may contribute to inflammatory infiltration and blood-brain barrier disruption. The work nominates candidate targets for mitigating secondary damage after stroke.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing with machine learning to identify chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets as key drivers of poor outcomes in ovarian cancer, particularly in residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The findings suggest that these inflammatory and fibroblast populations contribute to treatment resistance and adverse prognosis, highlighting potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors present Pasta, a transcriptomic aging clock trained with a novel 'age-shift' learning framework that predicts relative biological age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-seq and microarray data. Pasta's predictions align with senescence and stem-like states, and the clock was used to map chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation. This provides a versatile, platform-independent tool for studying aging biology.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial biology approaches, particularly spatial transcriptomics, are being applied to cancer epigenetics to study how local tissue context shapes regulatory programs in tumors. It argues that while bulk and single-cell sequencing have advanced tumor biology, they lose spatial information, and highlights the need to integrate spatial context into epigenetic studies of cancer.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: The authors developed a gentle hydrogen peroxide-based bleaching method that removes melanin pigment while preserving tissue for immunohistochemistry, enabling them to map the development of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye on a unified timeline. They combined this with marker staining (Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp, S100b, Cd34, Dct/Tyrp2) and reanalysis of published single-cell RNA-seq data to build a developmental atlas of pigmented ocular tissues.

papers.title: Condition-Associated Pattern Extraction and Recovery From Multi-Condition Single-Cell RNA-seq Data With CAPER.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in multi-condition single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data analysis is the disentanglement of true biological signals from unwanted variations in complex experimental designs. Current statistical and machine learning-based methods struggle with this task, often providing only visualizable embeddings, over-correcting and discarding biological signal, or failing to resolve cell-type-specific responses. Here, we present CAPER, a matrix factorization framework that explicitly disentangles shared biological states from condition-specific variations. CAPER directly outputs an
papers.summary: CAPER is a new matrix factorization framework for multi-condition single-cell RNA-seq data that explicitly separates shared biological states from condition-specific variation, rather than only producing visual embeddings or over-correcting and losing signal. It directly outputs interpretable condition-associated expression patterns and can recover cell-type-specific responses, addressing a key limitation of existing statistical and machine-learning approaches.

papers.title: Normalization choice drives biological interpretation in single-cell RNA-seq cancer studies: A systematic benchmarking of 465 computational pipelines.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed our understanding of tumor heterogeneity, yet the impact of computational pipeline choices on biological conclusions remains poorly characterized. Here, we systematically benchmark 465 combinations of 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer datasets encompassing over 434,000 cells. We introduce the Biological Discordance Score (BDS), a metric that quantifies how marker gene interpretation changes across pipelines. We find that normalization method choice has a greater impact on biological interpretation than clu
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 465 combinations of normalization methods and clustering algorithms across three cancer scRNA-seq datasets (over 434,000 cells) and introduces a Biological Discordance Score to quantify how pipeline choices alter marker-gene interpretation. The key finding is that normalization method choice affects biological conclusions more than clustering algorithm choice, meaning computational pipeline decisions can substantially change downstream interpretation in cancer single-cell studies.

papers.title: Molecular traces of microbial cross-kingdom migration: from the gut ecosystem to the intervertebral disc microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is strongly associated with its development. Recent studies have shown that the gut microbiota (GM) and its metabolites may be involved in the occurrence and development of IVDD through the gut-disc axis. However, the key microbes mediating this process and their specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: This study investigates the 'gut-disc axis' hypothesis, proposing that gut microbes and their metabolites migrate to intervertebral discs and contribute to disc degeneration (IVDD), a major cause of low back pain. The authors aim to identify key microbial species and molecular mechanisms mediating this cross-kingdom migration, though the abstract does not report specific findings.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomic Profiling of FAP-Positive Cells in Gastric Cancer and Association with Immunotherapy Efficacy.
papers.abstract: The spatial heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment in gastric cancer, particularly in the stromal compartment, remains poorly characterized. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-positive cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are known to promote tumor progression, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. However, the spatial transcriptional programs of FAP+ and FAP- stroma and their associations with response to immunotherapy are not fully understood.
papers.journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to profile FAP-positive versus FAP-negative stromal cells in gastric cancer, characterizing their distinct transcriptional programs within the tumor microenvironment. It further examines how these spatial stromal features associate with patient response to immunotherapy, highlighting FAP+ cancer-associated fibroblasts as potential mediators of immune evasion and treatment resistance.

papers.title: Bulk and single-cell analysis of FAM72D reveals its prognostic and functional relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Family with sequence similarity 72 member D (FAM72D) has been implicated in proliferative programs in several malignancies, but its clinical significance, cellular distribution and underlying biological programs in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain insufficiently characterized. FAM72D expression and its clinical relevance were evaluated using The Cancer Genome Atlas-liver hepatocellular carcinoma (TCGA-LIHC) cohort and three independent GEO cohorts. Cox regression, patient-level bootstrap validation, calibration analysis and decision curve analysis were used to assess its prognostic contri
papers.summary: This study analyzes FAM72D expression in hepatocellular carcinoma using TCGA and three independent GEO cohorts, combining bulk and single-cell data. It finds that FAM72D is associated with proliferative programs and has prognostic value in HCC, supported by Cox regression, bootstrap validation, calibration, and decision curve analysis.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis identifies monocyte/macrophage senescence-associated candidate genes in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive vascular disorder characterized by immune dysregulation and vascular remodeling. Cellular senescence modulates immune responses, but its role in PAH, particularly in monocytes/macrophages, remains unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify senescence-associated candidate genes associated with monocytes/macrophages in PAH.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic datasets to identify senescence-associated genes specifically in monocytes/macrophages in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). The authors propose candidate genes linking immune cell senescence to PAH vascular remodeling, though the abstract does not report experimental validation. The work is a bioinformatic prioritization of targets rather than a mechanistic or functional study.

papers.title: Patient classification using single-cell RNA-sequencing data with deep learning convolutional neural networks.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables gene expression profiling at the resolution of individual cells, revealing cellular heterogeneity that is obscured in bulk RNA-seq. While this offers a powerful lens to study disease-specific changes, leveraging scRNA-seq data for patient phenotype classification remains challenging due to limited sample numbers, cell count variability, high dimensionality, and dependence on cell-type annotations. Existing tools attempt to address these issues using probabilistic models or attention mechanisms, but face limitations in scalability, interpretability
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning convolutional neural network approach for classifying patient phenotypes directly from single-cell RNA-sequencing data. The method aims to overcome common challenges such as limited sample sizes, variable cell counts, high dimensionality, and reliance on cell-type annotations. It offers a potentially more scalable and interpretable alternative to existing probabilistic or attention-based tools.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis reveals the role of PGRN in modulating fibroblast heterogeneity and enhancing wound healing.
papers.abstract: The wound microenvironment plays a crucial role in the skin wound healing process. Fibroblasts, one of the critical cell types within this microenvironment, exhibit significant heterogeneity that influences healing outcomes. Previous studies have demonstrated that progranulin (PGRN) may reduce fibrogenesis during wound healing. However, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Thus, this study aims to investigate the specific effects of PGRN on fibroblast heterogeneity of skin wound healing in mice.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA-seq to examine how progranulin (PGRN) affects fibroblast heterogeneity during skin wound healing in mice. The authors find that PGRN modulates distinct fibroblast subpopulations, which may explain its previously observed anti-fibrotic effects and its ability to enhance healing outcomes.

papers.title: GlycoRNA-related cellular program scoring identifies Siglec- and myeloid-associated tumor microenvironments for glycoRNA validation.
papers.abstract: Glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) represent a recently recognized connection between RNA biology and cell-surface glycobiology. However, whether glycoRNA-related processes are relevant to human tumors remains unclear, partly because direct glycoRNA measurements are not yet available across large cancer cohorts. We therefore used transcriptomic data to identify tumor settings in which glycoRNA-related programs may be most suitable for further experimental validation.
papers.summary: The authors developed a transcriptomic scoring approach to infer glycoRNA-related cellular programs across human tumors, since direct glycoRNA measurement is not feasible in large cancer cohorts. They identified tumor microenvironments enriched for Siglec- and myeloid-associated signatures as the most promising settings for future experimental glycoRNA validation. This is a hypothesis-generating computational study that prioritizes cancer contexts for follow-up glycoRNA work.

papers.title: Integrated Multiomics and Functional Validation Identify CLSPN as a Central Integrator of Genomic Instability and Immune Remodeling in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by pervasive genomic instability, yet the molecular mechanisms linking replication stress responses to genome alteration and phenotypic evolution remain incompletely understood. Here, we performed an integrative multiomics analysis combined with functional validation to investigate the role of CLSPN, a key adaptor of the ATR-CHK1 pathway, in CRC. Machine learning-based feature selection identified CLSPN as a robust prognostic factor. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses revealed that CLSPN is preferentially enriched in highly proliferative tu
papers.summary: This study integrates multiomics data with functional experiments to show that CLSPN, a key adaptor in the ATR-CHK1 replication stress pathway, acts as a central hub linking genomic instability to immune remodeling in colorectal cancer. Machine learning identified CLSPN as a robust prognostic marker, and single-cell and spatial analyses showed it is enriched in highly proliferative tumor cells. The work positions CLSPN as a potential biomarker and mechanistic node connecting replication stress to the tumor immune microenvironment.

papers.title: Development and External Validation of an M2 Macrophage-Related Prognostic Signature in Breast Cancer Using Multi-Omics Data and Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), particularly the M2-like phenotype, are central regulators of breast cancer progression; however, clinically applicable models capturing their functional heterogeneity and biological mechanisms remain limited.
papers.summary: This study develops and externally validates a prognostic gene signature for breast cancer based on M2 macrophage-related genes, using multi-omics data and machine learning. The signature aims to capture the functional heterogeneity of tumor-associated macrophages and improve risk stratification for breast cancer patients.

papers.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Rora-Associated Aberrant Granulosa Cell Differentiation in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by follicular developmental arrest, yet the molecular basis underlying impaired granulosa cell (GC) differentiation remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics to profile granulosa cells in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), identifying aberrant differentiation states linked to the transcription factor Rora. The findings suggest that Rora-associated dysregulation of granulosa cell maturation contributes to the follicular developmental arrest characteristic of PCOS.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics combined with machine learning to unravel the heterogeneity of cholangiocarcinoma and the WFDC3-mediated prognostic regulatory mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) exhibits substantial cellular heterogeneity and a complex tumor microenvironment (TME), contributing to poor clinical outcomes. Effective prognostic biomarkers and a deeper understanding of the cellular ecosystems associated with high-risk disease remain urgently needed.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial multi-omics with machine learning to characterize cellular heterogeneity and the tumor microenvironment in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The authors identify WFDC3 as a key gene mediating prognostic regulatory mechanisms, linking specific cell populations to high-risk disease. The work aims to provide prognostic biomarkers and a deeper understanding of the cellular ecosystems underlying poor outcomes.

papers.title: Study on tumor ecology and precision medicine strategy of oral squamous cell carcinoma based on multi-omics cell atlas.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is characterized by inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity, which complicates patient stratification and treatment. Although single-cell studies have improved the resolution of the OSCC microenvironment, the relationships among cellular states, spatial organization, immune-repertoire dynamics, and patient-level ecosystem patterns remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study constructs a multi-omics single-cell atlas of oral squamous cell carcinoma to characterize tumor heterogeneity across cellular states, spatial organization, and immune-repertoire dynamics. The authors use this atlas to define patient-level 'ecosystem' patterns and propose a framework for precision medicine stratification. It extends single-cell resolution of the OSCC microenvironment toward integrated, ecosystem-level patient classification.

papers.title: Histopathology-guided spatial transcriptomic analysis identifies an ECM-associated stromal pattern in lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma with complementary proteomic and functional analyses.
papers.abstract: Lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC) is a rare but locally aggressive malignancy characterized by perineural invasion, recurrence, and limited systemic treatment options. Although extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of tumor progression, its spatial organization and functional relevance in LGACC remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study used histopathology-guided spatial transcriptomics on lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma, a rare and aggressive eye tumor, to map gene expression while preserving tissue location. The authors identified a distinct stromal pattern associated with extracellular matrix remodeling and supported it with complementary proteomic and functional experiments. The work suggests ECM-associated stromal features may contribute to LGACC progression and could be explored as future therapeutic targets.
